questions.q: Distinguish between primary and secondary data, and between census and sample methods of collection.

answer.text: Primary data are those collected first-hand by the investigator directly from the source for a specific enquiry, and so are original. Secondary data are those that have already been collected and processed by someone else, and are obtained from published sources such as the Census reports, government publications or newspapers. Primary data are more reliable and specific but costlier and more time-consuming to gather.

In the census, or complete enumeration, method, every single unit of the population is studied, as in the Population Census of India. In the sample method, only a representative part of the population, called a sample, is studied, and its results are used to draw conclusions about the whole. The census gives complete information but is costly and slow, while sampling saves time, money and effort, though it may involve some sampling error.

answer: Thus the choice depends on the purpose, resources and accuracy required.
